rules.title: FEHA source-of-income protections in tenant selection
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent, or apply different terms, based on how a tenant will pay rent (source of income). This includes Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance. Providers must also comply with assistance program requirements and may not advertise a preference such as "No Section 8."

exemption_conditions.condition: An owner who occupies the home and rents to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics, but still may not publish discriminatory statements, notices, or advertisements.

coverage.notes: Owner-occupant exemption applies only when renting to one additional person.

rules.coverage_text: Covers most housing providers and housing-related service providers in California, including landlords, tenant screening companies, and property managers, for most housing accommodations.
rules.exemptions: An owner who occupies the home and rents to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics. The owner still may not make discriminatory statements or advertisements.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act
rules.quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).

rules.title: FEHA criminal history limits in tenant screening
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice records, and may not impose blanket bans on people with criminal histories. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature, severity, and age of the offense.
rules.coverage_text: Covers housing providers in California, including landlords and tenant screening companies, when screening applicants.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act
rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.

llm.notes: CRD guidance page on FEHA. Most of the page covers general anti-discrimination rules, which were not recorded. I extracted the specific screening restrictions on source of income and criminal history. The page names no code section, so the citation is FEHA by name, and it gives no dates.
